interface.title: Speech Brain Viewer — Parallel and distributed speech encoding across human auditory cortex (Hamilton, Oganian, Hall & Chang, Cell 2021)
interface.field: Auditory and speech neuroscience; human intracranial electrophysiology (ECoG/sEEG in epilepsy patients)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploring published results: browsing per-electrode encoding models and stimulation-mapping outcomes that come with a paper
interface.what_it_is_for: Pick an intracranial electrode on a 3D left-hemisphere brain and see its speech receptive field under several acoustic and phonological encoding models, with its prediction correlation, or see what electrical stimulation at that site did to hearing and speech perception.

data.note: The app loads all data from the repo at startup: the brain and temporal-lobe surface meshes, electrode coordinates and anatomical labels, receptive-field weights for 7 models, correlation values, and stim_results.xlsx. No upload or demo button is needed. Electrode numbers I saw: 198, 210, 439, 316 and 4.

screens_never_reached: A stimulation result I could confirm came from a blue (Effect 1, sound hallucination) or red (Effect 3, complex) site. On the whole brain those sites sit behind the transparent mesh, and presses there landed on the mesh and rotated the view instead (screens/042.webp, screens/044.webp, screens/049.webp, screens/051.webp).
not_done: Plain clicks never selected an electrode in this headless browser. Selection only worked with a press-and-release (browser_drag), and even that sometimes rotated the brain without selecting anything, so electrode selection was unreliable here. The app itself asks for a click and uses clickData, so this is a browser-automation quirk, not the intended interaction.

Hover labels sometimes show the brain or temporal-lobe mesh trace with a leftover anatomical name (screens/023.webp), so the hovered trace is not always the dot. Per the app code, a selection reads clickData points[0]['id'] and only the electrode scatter sets ids, so clicks that land on the mesh select nothing; any panel update came from a dot.

The 'Electrode N' number in the panel title is an index into the filtered electrode array, not a fixed electrode ID. When I switched from Stimulation back to Receptive Fields, the panel showed 'Electrode 4, r=0.42' without a new selection (screens/054.webp): the stimulation-mode click id carried over and was read as a receptive-field electrode index.
The Anatomy colouring has no legend, so colours can only be matched to regions by hovering.

Did not use the 'Share chart', Pan, orbital-rotation or 3D zoom-mode buttons beyond briefly clicking Zoom mode, and did not follow the external Video Tutorial or paper links, which are outside the allowed server.
Did not reset the zoomed STRF axes (stopped at the action budget).
